sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks (all populated rows), especially A2:D2; Deterministic Checks (all populated rows); Internal Quality Checks A2:Z2 (no additional populated annotation or cell comment for row 1)
evidence: The actual frozen workbook Quality Checks!A2:D2 and Internal Quality Checks!A2:Z2 define a natural product request, with no row-1-specific annotation. The corresponding frozen quality-checks.md:9-11 asks for a cold reading and rejects acceptance lists, spec tables and build recipes. .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r2/task/instruction.md:1 opens with "I'd like a small playground for trying out browser ideas" and explains the workspace and shared-library purpose. Line 3 gives the concrete personal problem, "The annoying part is losing something that was working," then explains preview recovery and saved versions in user terms. Lines 5, 7 and 9 refer to the six notes, ordinary save/return and keyboard/mobile needs, and the delivery location. The complete instruction is 194 words in five prose paragraphs, with no numbered acceptance list, table, feature matrix, endpoint list, framework mandate or implementation algorithm. The technical start contract is in the separate integration note as the frozen template and TASK_AUTHORING_WORKFLOW.md section 2 prescribe; integration.md:3 explicitly leaves frontend tools open, integration.md:5 leaves routes/file layout open, and policy.md:5 leaves layout, labels, indentation, API routes and request fields open. All six notes were read for context. Hash verification of all 77 frozen task/rules files matched manifest inputs; raw evidence is at qc/runs/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r2/per-row-review/evidence/01/source-verification.json. This is a source-only wording verdict: no runtime evidence is required for row 1, and it makes no claim about app correctness, configured judging, Oracle, model score or portal clearance.
counterexample: Scope-specific thought experiments, not executed app runs: a static three-pane shell that loses a changed preview or cannot save could coexist with a naturally written brief, but it would violate instruction.md:1,3,7; row 1 does not certify that app or its grade. A conforming app built with a vanilla-JavaScript frontend and different control labels/routes is expressly permitted by integration.md:3,5 and policy.md:5, so the natural product request does not reject that alternative. Neither example exposes a row-1 wording defect.
